feature: Make Product Card Wishlist Button Always Visible on Touch
description: The wishlist button on product cards has opacity: 0 by default and only appears on hover. This makes it inaccessible on touch devices where there's no hover state.

phases.name: Implementation
phases.description: Add touch device support for wishlist button visibility

subtasks.title: Add media query for touch devices
subtasks.description: Add @media (hover: none) rule to _product-card.css to make the wishlist button always visible on touch devices. This media query targets devices that don't support hover (primarily touch devices).
acceptance_criteria: Media query @media (hover: none) is added to the CSS file
Within the media query, .product-card-wishlistBtn has opacity: 1 and transform: scale(1)
The media query is placed after the existing hover rules for proper CSS cascade
subtasks.notes: Added @media (hover: none) media query to _product-card.css. The media query sets opacity: 1 and transform: scale(1) for .product-card-wishlistBtn, making the wishlist button always visible on touch devices. Placed after existing hover rules for proper CSS cascade.

subtasks.title: Verify CSS syntax and placement
subtasks.description: Ensure the CSS is syntactically correct and properly integrated with the existing styles
acceptance_criteria: CSS file has no syntax errors
subtasks.notes: Verified CSS implementation. All acceptance criteria met: CSS syntax is correct, media query is properly structured at lines 141-146, and there are no conflicts with existing styles. The @media (hover: none) query is well-placed after hover rules for proper cascade and integrates cleanly with the existing wishlist button styles.

files_to_modify.description: Add @media (hover: none) query to show wishlist button on touch devices

technical_details.css_approach: Using @media (hover: none) media query which targets devices without hover capability. This is the modern, standards-based approach supported by all major browsers.
technical_details.alternative_considered: @media (pointer: coarse) was also considered, but @media (hover: none) is more semantically accurate for this use case since we specifically want to handle the absence of hover support.

final_acceptance: Wishlist button is visible on touch devices without needing hover
Wishlist button still shows on hover for desktop devices
No visual regressions on desktop browsers
